preamble: Devoicing of the breathy-voiced (voiced aspirated) bilabial plosive [bʱ] to the voiceless aspirated [pʰ] keeps the place of articulation and the aspiration while removing vocal-fold vibration. It is the classic Greek reflex of Proto-Indo-European *bʰ (PIE *bʰéreti > Ancient Greek φέρω [pʰérɔː]), and it occurred independently in Romani, where Old Indo-Aryan bh, dh, gh became ph, th, kh. Punjabi instead turned initial bʱ into unaspirated [p] plus low tone, and the Dardic languages simply lost the breathy voice (bʱ > b), so they belong to other cells.

examples.note: Via Proto-Hellenic *pʰérō; the PIE voiced aspirates *bʰ, *dʰ, *gʰ became the voiceless aspirates φ, θ, χ.
Same correspondence; the aspirate later became the fricative [f] in post-classical Greek.
Via Proto-Hellenic *pʰāgós; cognate with Latin fāgus and English beech.
Word-internal *bʰ shows the same outcome; cognate with Latin nebula.
Devoicing of the voiced aspirates bh, dh, gh to ph, th, kh is one of the developments that set Romani apart from the other Indo-Aryan languages.
Same development; some modern dialects are now losing aspiration (ph > p).

sources: Matras, Y. (2002). Romani: A Linguistic Introduction. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511486791
